Lemma
[Hopf's Lemma] ↗ def:uniform-ellipticity ↗ thm:weak-maximum-principle-c-zero 1. ch6:6.4-lem-1\group Maximum Principles

Assume $u \in C^2(U) \cap C^1( ar U)$ and \[ c = 0 \quad ext{in } U. \] Suppose further \[ Lu \leq 0 \quad ext{in } U, \] and there exists a point $x^0 \in \partial U$ such that \[ (14) \qquad u(x^0) > u(x) \quad ext{for all } x \in U. \] Assume finally that $U$ satisfies the interior ball condition at $x^0$; that is, there exists an open ball $B \subset U$ with $x^0 \in \partial B$.

(i) Then \[ rac{\partial u}{\partial u }(x^0) > 0, \] where $ u $ is the outer unit normal to $B$ at $x^0$.

(ii) If \[ c \geq 0 \quad ext{in } U, \] the same conclusion holds provided \[ u(x^0) \geq 0. \]

Proof

\sketch Use the exponential radial barrier $v=e^{-\lambda |x|^2}-e^{-\lambda r^2}$ on an interior annulus. For large $\lambda $, ellipticity gives $Lv\le 0$; comparison with $u+\varepsilon v-u(x^0)$ and differentiation at $x^0$ yield a strictly positive outer normal derivative.

□
